newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sky is the limit for bullish Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Sky is the limit for bullish Brussels bourse.

text.p: The Brussels bourse moved quietly but determinedly higher on a thinly-traded Wednesday, and traders said there was no end in sight to the rally that has pushed the market up 20 percent so far this year.
"All the economic statistics point to a very good climate for equities," one trader said.

Traders said the performance of the Dow Jones Industrial Average, the firm dollar and low long-term interest rates all pointed to a continuing bull run in Brussels and elsewhere despite some signs of nerves that the party would have to come to an end sooner or later.
The Bel-20 blue chip share index ended the day 4.76 points or 0.21 percent higher at 2,247.70 with some 2.5 billion francs of Belgian shares changing hands.
The index has risen, with one serious and several very minor corrections, in almost a straight line from 1,871.05 on January 2.
Oil major PetroFina was again the busiest share by value, ending unchanged at 12,925 francs in a volume of more than 30,000 shares.
The rise followed positive remarks at the company's annual meeting on Monday.
The strongest percentage risers in the index were electronics firm Barco, up 1.7 percent to 6,600 francs, and Kredietbank, also up 1.7 percent at 13,675 francs.
Traders said the Barco rise was largely speculative, while the KB rise was a technical rebound from recent weakness.

Biggest loser outside the index was fast food chain Quick, down 6.6 percent to 1,905 francs after the company said in a newspaper interview the first quarter of the year had been flat. Parent GIB also suffered, falling 3.2 percent to 1,510 francs.
